logp.method_description: To measure the partition coefficient of the selected three gold complexes using a ‘‘shake-flask’’ method, a two phase system composed of n-octanol and deionised water was used.63 The stock solutions of the selected gold complexes (sample preparation) were diluted with water to the concentration of 1  104 M and this solution was used for further investigation. 3 ml of this diluted stock solution was mixed with 3 ml of n-octanol and shaken using a mechanical shaker at 25 1C (Orbital ShakerIncubator ES-20, Grant-bio) for 30 minutes at 250 rpm, centrifuged (Centrifuge 5702, Eppendorf) at 3000 rpm for 20 minutes to afford complete phase separation, and the n-octanol phase was removed. The absorbance of the aqueous phase was measured spectrophotometrically at 320 nm for complexes 1 and 3 and at 270 nm for complex 2, respectively, and used for the determination of the concentration of gold complexes left in the aqueous phase. A calibration curve was obtained from a series of different, but known concentrations of gold complex water solution.P values were calculated using eqn (2): P = ((y - x) / x) × (Vaq / Voct) where P is the partition coefficient; y is the total concentration of gold complexes, x is the concentration of gold complexes in the aqueous phase; Vaq is the volume of aqueous phase; andVoct is the volume of n-octanol.
